headline: Distinguish Town Lodging from National Park Camping
reservation: Reservations for lodging in Teton Village or Jackson are separate from National Park Service campground bookings. Grand Teton campgrounds utilize a rolling window on a centralized federal platform, while private resorts manage their own inventories. Always verify if your specific dates require a backcountry permit for overnight stays.

days.title: Valley Scenic Corridor

stops.name: Taggart Lake
stops.detail: Hike through sagebrush flats and aspen groves to reach a clear glacial lake at the foot of the Grand Teton.

stops.name: Oxbow Bend
stops.detail: Observe the slow-moving section of the Snake River where Mount Moran reflects in the water and wildlife may be present near the banks.

days.driving: Allow 3 hours for the valley traverse; conditions vary
days.note: Expect slower speeds near the Moose-Wilson road due to narrow lanes and potential wildlife sightings.

days.title: High Elevation Views

stops.name: Jackson Hole Mountain Resort Aerial Tram
stops.detail: Ride to the summit of Rendezvous Mountain for 360-degree views of the valley and the southern Tetons.

stops.name: Corbet's Cabin
stops.detail: Visit this high-altitude landmark at the tram summit for a unique perspective on the surrounding granite peaks.

days.driving: Minimal driving if staying in Teton Village; allow for walking to base
days.note: Tram operations are seasonal and highly dependent on wind and weather conditions.

days.title: Historical Vistas and River Flats

stops.name: Menors Ferry Historic District
stops.detail: Learn about 19th-century river crossings and visit the Chapel of the Transfiguration for its framed mountain view.

stops.name: Blacktail Ponds Overlook
stops.detail: Scan the marshy bottomlands for moose or waterfowl during the quieter morning hours.

days.driving: Allow 1.5 hours for local stops; conditions vary
days.note: Check official maps for the seasonal closure status of any secondary gravel access roads.

intel.title: Village and Park Limits
intel.text: Teton Village offers structured parking but can fill during peak event weekends or winter ski days. In the park, parking in non-designated roadside areas is strictly prohibited to protect vegetation.

intel.title: Digital Preparedness
intel.text: Expect total loss of signal in the canyons and near the base of the peaks. Use GPS-enabled maps that do not require data to navigate the trail networks.

intel.title: Valley Logistics
intel.text: The distance between the town of Jackson and the northern park boundary at Signal Mountain is significant. Top off your fuel in Jackson or Wilson before starting a full day of park exploration.

intel.title: Mountain Weather Pacing
intel.text: Afternoon thunderstorms are common in July and August. Plan to be off high ridges and open water before midday to avoid lightning risks.

intel.title: Moose-Wilson Road Restrictions
intel.text: This corridor is often subject to construction or wildlife-related closures. Check the current status at the Moose Entrance Station before attempting to use it as a throughway.

plan.arrival: Land at JAC and pick up your vehicle; stop in the town of Jackson for bear spray and groceries before heading to Teton Village or park lodges.
plan.vehicle: SUVs are popular but not required for paved park roads; check with rental agencies regarding the use of 4WD on Forest Service access routes.
plan.goldenHour: Signal Mountain Summit offers a panoramic sunset view of the entire range, provided the road is clear of snow.
